sections.heading: C2 — State Laws and Rules
sections.markdown:
## C2 — State Laws and Rules

FACT_ID: sec02-R01 | anchor: A20
A Maine-registered motor vehicle needs a current Maine inspection before use on a public road. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R02 | anchor: A20
The required vehicle inspection occurs annually at an official inspection station. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R03 | anchor: A20
A missing current inspection sticker can bring a fine and a driver-license point consequence. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R04 | anchor: A20
Police may inspect a vehicle’s safety at any time. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R05 | anchor: A20
A driving examination is refused if the vehicle fails regular criteria, has an inoperative door or an insecure seat, or has a glove-compartment door that does not stay securely closed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R06 | anchor: A20
The vehicle identification number must remain visible and must not be removed or altered. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R07 | anchor: A20
An inspection-ready rearview mirror must be clear and intact, without cracks or sharp edges. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R08 | anchor: A20
The horn must be audible from 200 feet. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R09 | anchor: A20
Wipers and their blades must work properly. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R10 | anchor: A20
A functioning defroster needs an operating fan that sends heated air onto the windshield. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R11 | anchor: A20
Turn signals, headlights, rear lamps, brake lamps and the plate lamp must function, with lenses of the correct type and color. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R12 | anchor: A20
A vehicle needs both a foot brake and a parking brake. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R13 | anchor: A20
The foot brake must stop a vehicle traveling 20 miles per hour within 30 feet. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R14 | anchor: A20
The parking brake must hold the vehicle on a hill. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R15 | anchor: A20
The windshield and windows must not be cracked, broken, cloudy or obstructed. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R16 | anchor: A20
Steering and front-end components must work properly without excessive wear. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R17 | anchor: A20
The exhaust system must have no holes or leaks and must avoid excessive noise. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R18 | anchor: A20
Fuel-system parts must be free of holes and leaks. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R19 | anchor: A20
Noncommercial vehicle tires need at least 2/32 inch of tread and no cuts, tears or dangerous defects. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R20 | anchor: A20
Every issued registration plate must be attached to the vehicle and readable. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R21 | anchor: A20
Body and chassis parts must be present without rust, sharp edges or other defects. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R22 | anchor: A20
The speedometer and odometer must function and must not be altered or tampered with. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R23 | anchor: A20
The fuel inlet must remain unmodified. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R24 | anchor: A20
The catalytic converter must be correctly installed and unmodified. [A20]
Source: [A20 -> pdf-0020]

FACT_ID: sec02-R25 | anchor: A21
Replace burned-out headlight bulbs and clean dirty lenses, which can reduce night vision by more than half. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R26 | anchor: A21
Replace signal- or brake-light bulbs and fuses as needed so other drivers can see your intended actions. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R27 | anchor: A21
Clean vehicle glass on both sides to reduce glare and improve visibility. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R28 | anchor: A21
Look for worn tire tread and check tire pressure while the tires are cold, before substantial driving. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R29 | anchor: A21
Check that the brake pedal stays well above the floor, and watch for scraping, squealing or pulling to one side during braking. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R30 | anchor: A21
Steering-wheel movement of 2 inches or more without a vehicle response indicates excessive play. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R31 | anchor: A21
Check wiper wear and contact tension, keep washer fluid full, and use antifreeze washer fluid in winter. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R32 | anchor: A21
Have a mechanic check exhaust noise, rattling or rust on the muffler or tailpipe. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R33 | anchor: A21
Carbon monoxide in gasoline-engine exhaust is deadly and odorless, with possible weariness, headache, dizziness, nausea and ringing ears. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R34 | anchor: A21
Prolonged breathing of carbon monoxide can be fatal. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R35 | anchor: A21
A gasoline-powered vehicle may not be driven on a public road if its exhaust produces visible smoke, other than water vapor, for more than 5 consecutive seconds. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R36 | anchor: A21
Keep the gauges working so they can warn of problems such as overheating or low oil pressure. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R37 | anchor: A21
After pressing down on the vehicle’s front or rear, more than 2 bounces can indicate a need for new shock absorbers. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R38 | anchor: A21
Worn shock absorbers can make staying in the lane difficult on curves. [A21]
Source: [A21 -> pdf-0021]

FACT_ID: sec02-R39 | anchor: A22
Regular vehicle checks should include engine oil, coolant, transmission fluid, brake fluid and fan-belt wear and tightness. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R40 | anchor: A22
The manual recommends oil changes every 3,000 to 5,000 miles and periodic engine tune-ups to help prevent common vehicle problems. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R41 | anchor: A22
Recommended emergency equipment includes the owner’s manual, spare tire, jack, lug wrench, first-aid kit, blanket, flashlight and road maps. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R42 | anchor: A22
On a public road, vehicle audio heard from more than 25 feet away and exceeding 85 decibels is prohibited. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R43 | anchor: A22
Vehicle audio on a public road is also prohibited at an unreasonable volume considering the vehicle’s location and its effect on nearby people. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R44 | anchor: A22
An excessive vehicle-audio violation is a traffic infraction carrying $50 for a first offense. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R45 | anchor: A22
A second excessive vehicle-audio offense carries a $100 assessment. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]

FACT_ID: sec02-R46 | anchor: A22
A third or later excessive vehicle-audio offense carries a $150 assessment. [A22]
Source: [A22 -> pdf-0022]
